What is real

Every identifier, wait, tier, destination and state was read off the running prototype at /mockups/ward-flow/ed/rph-ed on 2026-09-04. Department and ward names come from ward-sites.ts.

What is invented

The layout, the bar lengths as a proportion of the 24-hour target, and the next action on each decision. The underlying figures are the screen's own.

Two different clocks

Coming in is measured from the referral; going out from when the move became owed. They are drawn on separate axes and never ranked against one another, because they are not the same quantity.

Beds this team has asked for

0

Nothing can be listed here, and that is a gap in the record rather than a quiet week. A referral stores that its source was a community service, but not which team raised it — so a referral Midland sent to an emergency department or a ward cannot be traced back to Midland by anything in the model. Until the record carries the team, this list would be a guess.

Where these teams come from

Every team listed comes from one extracted source document, no team has agreed to be represented, and nothing here has been checked against a real service. The names are real; no contact detail is held, and none is invented.

What is invented

Every patient, bed and date. The suburb count and the sixteen team names are real. Durations are shown and calendar dates never are, so nothing drifts with the real calendar.

Not a caseload

An empty list means nobody has been recorded as followed up, not that nobody is being followed up. This page must never be read as a record of who a team is looking after.
